What variables in the raw data is `output` *Tongue y-position* derived from?\n\ni. From `acquisition['BehavioralTimeSeries'].time_series['Camera0_side_TongueTracking']`, whose\n`data` is `(n_frames, 3)` = (`tongue_x`, `tongue_y`, `tongue_likelihood`) with matching\n`timestamps` (~300 Hz). Column 1 (`tongue_y`) provides the value and column 2 (the DeepLabCut\nlikelihood) decides visibility. `trials.start_time` is also used, to bucket each frame into the\ntrial it was acquired in. If the series is absent the output falls back to all \"not visible\"\n(it is in fact present in all 174 sessions).\n\nii.\n```python\n    bts = nwb.acquisition.get('BehavioralTimeSeries', None)\n    if bts is None or 'Camera0_side_TongueTracking' not in bts.time_series:\n        return out, 0.0\n\n    ts_obj = bts.time_series['Camera0_side_TongueTracking']\n    frame_t = np.asarray(ts_obj.timestamps[:], dtype=np.float64)\n    data = np.asarray(ts_obj.data[:, 1:3], dtype=np.float64)     # y, likelihood\n    y = data[:, 0]\n    visible = data[:, 1] > TONGUE_LIKELIHOOD_THRESH\n```\n\niii. Step 5 mapping: reference analogue `tracking.camera_0_side.tongue_y` (the marker stream\nused by `align_markers.py`). This is the only tongue measurement in the file. Step 4 records\nthat the AI checked availability across all 174 sessions and explained why the method paper\nused only 105–106 sessions (it additionally required usable *raw* video and all 8 markers\nincluding whisker), concluding that no session needs to be dropped for this output.\n\n## 8-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Tongue y-position*?\n\ni. Four steps, all in `bin_tongue()`:\n1. Frames with DeepLabCut likelihood ≤ 0.9 are discarded — when the tongue is retracted the\n   tracker still reports a position, so those frames are not real measurements.\n2. Every frame is bucketed into the trial it was acquired in\n   (`searchsorted(trial_start, frame_t, 'right') - 1`), and frames belonging to trials that\n   were dropped by curation are discarded. A frame can therefore only contribute to *its own*\n   trial's window, never to a neighbour's.\n3. Surviving visible frames are mapped to `(trial, bin)` cells and the mean `y` per cell is\n   computed with two `np.bincount` calls (sums / counts).\n4. A cell with no visible frame stays NaN, which becomes the \"not visible\" class in\n   `discretise_tongue`.\n\nii.\n```python\nTONGUE_LIKELIHOOD_THRESH = 0.9   # DeepLabCut likelihood above which the tongue is \"visible\"\n```\n```python\n    # frame -> trial (video only runs within a trial; frames start at trial_start)\n    frame_trial = np.searchsorted(trial_start, frame_t, side='right') - 1\n\n    # only visible frames matter for the value; keep them and their trial/bin index\n    vis = np.flatnonzero(visible & (frame_trial >= 0))\n    ...\n    pos_of_trial = np.full(n_raw, -1, dtype=np.int64)\n    pos_of_trial[keep_idx] = np.arange(n_trials)\n    pos = pos_of_trial[ft]\n    sel = pos >= 0\n    vis, pos = vis[sel], pos[sel]\n    ...\n    bin_idx = np.floor((rel - OFF_START) / BIN_SIZE).astype(np.int64)\n    np.clip(bin_idx, 0, NBINS - 1, out=bin_idx)\n    flat = pos * NBINS + bin_idx\n    n_cells = n_trials * NBINS\n    sums = np.bincount(flat, weights=y[vis], minlength=n_cells)\n    cnts = np.bincount(flat, minlength=n_cells)\n    with np.errstate(invalid='ignore', divide='ignore'):\n        mean = np.where(cnts > 0, sums / np.maximum(cnts, 1), np.nan)\n    out = mean.reshape(n_trials, NBINS)\n```\n\niii. Step 5 decision 10: \"The likelihood distribution is strongly bimodal (≈ 3–6 × 10⁻⁵ vs\n≈ 1.0); any threshold in [0.1, 0.99] gives the same answer to within 0.1% of frames\", so the\nexact cut is immaterial — ~6–11% of frames have the tongue visible. Step 10 Check 5, item 8\ngives the rationale for the trial bucketing: \"frames are first bucketed by trial … so a window\nthat extends past its own trial boundary cannot pick up a neighbouring trial's frames.\" Step 3\nrecords the reference's treatment (\"when the tongue was occluded while it was in the mouth …\nwe set the tongue position to its mean value\") and the AI's reading that occlusion is thereby\nan explicit distinct state, matching the required \"not visible\" class; the AI argues in Step 10\nCheck 3(f) that an explicit class \"is the more informative encoding of the same fact\" than the\nreference's mean imputation. `np.bincount` aggregation is also a Step 6 speed-up\n(~50× vs a per-bin loop).\n\n## 8-c. How is `output` *Tongue y-position* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. Per session, the 40th and 60th percentiles are taken over *all visible binned values* of that\nsession's retained trials (i.e. the non-NaN entries of the `(n_trials, 80)` bin-mean array —\nthe same quantity that is being discretised). Each bin is then labelled 0 if its value is\nstrictly below the 40th percentile, 2 if strictly above the 60th, 1 otherwise, and 3 if it has\nno visible frame. The two percentile values are stored per session in\n`metadata['session_info'][i]['tongue_pct_40_60']`. Resulting distribution across the dataset:\n0.098 / 0.049 / 0.098 / 0.755, i.e. exactly 40 : 20 : 40 of the visible bins.\n\nii.\n```python\nTONGUE_LOW_PCT = 40              # percentile boundaries for the tongue-y discretisation\nTONGUE_HIGH_PCT = 60\n```\n```python\ndef discretise_tongue(tongue_y):\n    \"\"\"Discretise tongue y into 0/1/2 by session percentiles, 3 where not visible.\"\"\"\n    cls = np.full(tongue_y.shape, 3, dtype=np.int64)\n    vis = ~np.isnan(tongue_y)\n    if vis.sum() == 0:\n        return cls, (np.nan, np.nan)\n    vals = tongue_y[vis]\n    p_lo = np.percentile(vals, TONGUE_LOW_PCT)\n    p_hi = np.percentile(vals, TONGUE_HIGH_PCT)\n    v = tongue_y[vis]\n    c = np.ones(v.shape, dtype=np.int64)\n    c[v < p_lo] = 0\n    c[v > p_hi] = 2\n    cls[vis] = c\n    return cls, (float(p_lo), float(p_hi))\n```\n```python\nOUTPUT_VALUES = [\n    ...\n    ['low (<40th pct)', 'mid (40-60th pct)', 'high (>60th pct)', 'not visible'],\n]\n```\n\niii. Step 5 decision 11: \"Tongue percentiles are computed per session over the *binned, visible*\nvalues of all retained trials of that session (the quantity actually being discretised)\" — the\nper-session scope and the 40/60 split come straight from the instructions, and taking the\npercentiles of the binned rather than the raw-frame values keeps the edges on the same\nquantity that is classified. Frames where the tongue is retracted are excluded first, because\nincluding them would shift the percentiles and mix noise with real protrusions. Sanity check 16\nverifies the 40 : 20 : 40 split of visible bins (`np.allclose`, atol 0.02, 5 sessions), check 15\nre-derives `output[3]` from the raw DLC timestamps/likelihoods exactly (32 bin probes per\nsession), and check 17 verifies visibility is concentrated after the go cue. The\n`--show-processing` panels 6–7 plot the y histogram with the two percentile lines and the class\nraster.\n\n## 8-d. How is `output` *Tongue y-position* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. Camera timestamps are on the same session-absolute clock as the spikes and the go cues, so\neach visible frame's offset from its trial's go cue is computed directly\n(`rel = frame_t - go[pos]`), frames outside `[-2.5, +1.5)` are dropped, and the remainder are\nassigned to bins by `floor((rel - OFF_START) / BIN_SIZE)` — the same go-cue-relative 50 ms grid\nused for the firing rates. The bin index is clipped to `[0, 79]` as a guard. No interpolation\nor offset correction is applied. Bins with no frames (including the leading bins of the ~3% of\ntrials whose go cue falls less than 2.5 s after trial start, where the trial-gated video has not\nstarted) end up in the \"not visible\" class.\n\nii.\n```python\n    rel = frame_t[vis] - go[pos]\n    inwin = (rel >= OFF_START) & (rel < OFF_END)\n    vis, pos, rel = vis[inwin], pos[inwin], rel[inwin]\n    ...\n    bin_idx = np.floor((rel - OFF_START) / BIN_SIZE).astype(np.int64)\n    np.clip(bin_idx, 0, NBINS - 1, out=bin_idx)\n    flat = pos * NBINS + bin_idx\n```\n\niii. Step 10 Check 3(c): \"subtract `BehavioralEvents['go_start_times'].timestamps` from both\nspike times and video timestamps\" — the same operation the reference `align_markers.py`\nperforms. Because both streams use one shared grid, bin *k* of the tongue output covers the\nsame interval as bin *k* of the firing rates by construction. Sanity check 15 recomputes the\nclass of specific `(trial, bin)` cells directly from the raw timestamps and matches exactly,\nand check 17 confirms the expected physiology (tongue visibility concentrated after the go cue,\nratio > 2), which is a direct test that the alignment has no temporal offset.\n\n## 9. How are minor mistakes in the data, e.g. missing data, handled?\n\ni. Nine distinct cases, each handled explicitly:\n- **Session never quality-controlled** (`classification`/`anno_name` all NaN): no unit matches\n  `'good'`, so the session returns `None` and is dropped (1 session).\n- **Trials outside the ephys recording** (`obs_intervals` shorter than the trials table,\n  9 sessions): located in the trials table by `start_time` and excluded; the AI refused the\n  \"first N trials\" shortcut because one session is not a prefix, and asserts the match.\n- **Trials with no spikes at all** (recording stopped mid-trial): detected post-binning and\n  dropped (2 trials), rather than emitted as 4 s of 0 Hz.\n- **Bins with no visible tongue frame**: represented as an explicit fourth class (3, \"not\n  visible\") rather than imputed.\n- **Missing tongue tracking series**: falls back to an all-NaN array → all \"not visible\".\n- **Units with a missing CCF x coordinate**: hemisphere falls back to the probe insertion's\n  targeted hemisphere.\n- **Unmapped CCF annotation strings**: warn and fall back to `OtherCortex` (all 293 strings\n  present were verified to map, so this never fires).\n- **Photostim start/stop count mismatch**: warn and leave the photostim input at 0.\n- **Go-cue count ≠ trials-table length**: hard `RuntimeError` (never triggered).\nAdditionally, `_worker` catches any per-session exception and prints a traceback rather than\naborting the whole run, and sessions with fewer than 2 surviving trials are dropped.\n\nii.\n```python\n        classification = np.asarray(units['classification'][:])\n        good = np.flatnonzero(classification == 'good')\n        if len(good) == 0:\n            io.close()\n            return None\n```\n```python\n        obs_trial = np.searchsorted(trial_start, obs[:, 0] - 1e-6)\n        if not np.allclose(trial_start[obs_trial], obs[:, 0]):\n            raise RuntimeError(f'{session_id}: obs_intervals do not match the trials table')\n```\n```python\n        nonempty = fr.sum(axis=(0, 2)) > 0\n        if not nonempty.all():\n            ...\n            fr = fr[:, nonempty, :]\n```\n```python\n        missing = np.isnan(elec_x)\n        if missing.any():\n            hemisphere[missing] = np.array([t.split(' ')[0] for t in probe_target])[missing]\n\n        region_name = np.array([annotation_to_region(a, t) for a, t in zip(anno, probe_target)])\n        unknown = region_name == None  # noqa: E711\n        if unknown.any():\n            print(f'  WARNING {session_id}: {unknown.sum()} units with unmapped annotation ...')\n            region_name[unknown] = 'OtherCortex'\n```\n```python\ndef _worker(args):\n    path, debug = args\n    try:\n        return process_session(path, collect_debug=debug)\n    except Exception as exc:          # keep one bad file from killing the whole run\n        import traceback\n        traceback.print_exc()\n        print(f'  ERROR processing {path}: {exc}', flush=True)\n        return None\n```\n\niii. Bins that fall outside the recorded interval\nare binned anyway and therefore read 0 Hz.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef bin_spikes_rate(spike_times, go_times):\n    \"\"\"Spike counts of one unit in the fixed window around every go cue, as a rate.\n    ...\n        Bin k covers [go + BIN_EDGES[k], go + BIN_EDGES[k+1]).\n    \"\"\"\n    edges = go_times[:, None] + BIN_EDGES[None, :]           # (n_trials, NBINS+1)\n    idx = np.searchsorted(spike_times, edges.ravel(), side='left')\n    idx = idx.reshape(edges.shape)\n    counts = np.diff(idx, axis=1)\n    return (counts / BIN_SIZE).astype(np.float32)\n```\n\niii. Step 5 decision 3 and Step 10 Check 3(d): rates in Hz (counts / 0.05 s) reproduce the\nreference `sliding_histogram(..., rate=True)`, which returns `binSpikes / bin_width`. The AI\ndocuments that the counting rule, the rate normalisation and the treatment of the trial edges\n(bin the whole fixed window regardless of when the trial ended, as `process_one_area` does) are\nidentical to the reference; only the bin width and stride differ, because the task\nspecification prescribes 50 ms non-overlapping bins instead of the reference's 40 ms/3.4 ms\nsliding window. Sanity check 2 re-counted the rates bin-by-bin from the raw NWB with a\nbrute-force `np.sum((st >= lo) & (st < hi)) / 0.05` and passed with `np.allclose` on 5 sessions\n× 20 trial×neuron probes; check 3 confirmed the per-neuron mean rates correlate at r = 0.988–\n0.998 with the independent `units.avg_firing_rate` column.\n\n## 2-c. How is the `neural` data filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Only units with `units/classification == 'good'` are kept. No threshold is applied to any\nindividual quality metric, and in particular the method paper's \"mean firing rate ≥ 2 Hz\"\ncriterion is deliberately **not** applied. A session with zero good units is dropped entirely.\nThis retains 69,453 of the ~272 k units (mean 401.5 per session, range 90–923) across 173\nsessions and 655 insertions.\n\nii.\n```python\n        units = nwb.units\n        classification = np.asarray(units['classification'][:])\n        good = np.flatnonzero(classification == 'good')\n        if len(good) == 0:\n            io.close()\n            return None\n```\n\n```python\n            'neuron_curation': (\n                \"units.classification == 'good' (region-specific logistic-regression QC \"\n                'classifiers of Chen, Liu et al. 2023 white paper); no firing-rate threshold'),\n```\n\niii. Step 3/Step 5 decision 4: `classification` is the output of the region-specific\nlogistic-regression QC classifiers described in `ChenLiuEtAl2023_SpikeSortingQC.pdf`, and is\nthe same criterion as the reference code's `qc_mode='classifier'` unit index. The AI rejected\nthe method paper's ≥ 2 Hz cut because \"it was introduced to stabilise per-neuron R² estimates\nin the video→firing-rate regression, not for decoding, and discarding low-rate neurons would\nthrow away decodable information\" — and the method paper itself states the result is\ninsensitive to that threshold. Consistency evidence in Step 4/Step 9: dropping the one session\nwith zero good units (`SC017_20190216_162508_s4`, whose `classification` column is NaN\nthroughout) yields exactly the paper's 173 sessions **and** exactly 655 insertions; the unit\ntotal of 69,453 is 99.3% of the published 69,943, attributed to the DANDI release version\npost-dating the paper snapshot.\n\n## 2-d. How is the per-trial `neural` data aligned to the event described in the `instructions`?\n\ni. Alignment is to **go-cue onset**, `BehavioralEvents['go_start_times'].timestamps`, one per\ntrial. Spike times and event timestamps are already on the same session-absolute clock, so no\nresampling, interpolation or per-stream offset correction is needed: the fixed grid of bin\nedges relative to the go cue is simply added to each retained trial's go-cue time, and the\nspikes are binned against those absolute edges. The same go-cue-relative grid is reused for the\ntwo inputs and for the tongue output, so bin *k* covers the same interval in every stream.\n\nii.\n```python\n        go_times = _events(nwb, 'go_start_times')\n        ...\n        go = go_times[keep_idx]\n```\n\n```python\n    edges = go_times[:, None] + BIN_EDGES[None, :]           # (n_trials, NBINS+1)\n    idx = np.searchsorted(spike_times, edges.ravel(), side='left')\n```\n\n```python\n            'temporal_alignment_event': 'onset of the auditory go cue (go_start_times)',\n            'off_start': OFF_START,\n            'off_end': OFF_END,\n```\n\niii. Step 5 decision 1: \"Alignment = go cue … Matches both papers and all reference code.\"\nStep 10 Check 3(c) records that the reference `.mat` export already stores spike times relative\nto `task_cue_time[0]` (the go cue) and aligns markers by subtracting the same quantity\n(`align_markers.py`), so subtracting `go_start_times` from the NWB absolute times is the same\noperation. The `--show-processing` plot panel 1 was used to verify alignment visually: trial\nstart sits at a median −3.2 s and the tone onset at exactly −1.85 s (= 0.65 s sample + 1.2 s\ndelay) on nearly every trial, which is the expected task geometry.\n\n## 2-e. What is the temporal resolution (time bin size) of the converted data? Is any temporal rebinning applied?\n\ni. 50 ms, i.e. 80 non-overlapping bins spanning −2.5 s to +1.5 s relative to the go cue. The\ngrid is defined once at module level as 81 edges (and 80 centres) relative to the go cue and\nreused for every trial, every session and every data stream, so every trial has exactly 80\ntimepoints. No rebinning/resampling of an intermediate representation is performed — spikes go\nstraight from raw times into the 50 ms bins, and the tongue video (~300 Hz) is averaged into the\nsame 50 ms bins in one step. `metadata['time_bin_size']` is 50.0 ms and the bin centres are\nstored in `metadata['bin_centers_s']`.\n\nii.\n```python\nOFF_START = -2.5          # s, signed time from the go cue to the start of the trial window\nOFF_END = 1.5             # s, signed time from the go cue to the end of the trial window\nBIN_SIZE = 0.05           # s\nNBINS = int(round((OFF_END - OFF_START) / BIN_SIZE))          # 80\nBIN_EDGES = OFF_START + BIN_SIZE * np.arange(NBINS + 1)       # (81,)\nBIN_CENTERS = BIN_EDGES[:-1] + BIN_SIZE / 2                   # (80,)\n```\n\n```python\n            'time_bin_size': BIN_SIZE * 1000.0,       # ms\n            'n_time_bins': NBINS,\n            'bin_centers_s': BIN_CENTERS.tolist(),\n```\n\niii. Step 5 decision 2: the window and bin width are taken verbatim from the Decoder Task\nsection of the instructions. Step 9/Step 10 Check 3(d) records this as a *deliberate* departure\nfrom the reference's 40 ms width / 3.4 ms stride sliding window, justified because the task\nspecifies the binning; a single fixed grid is also what makes the \"same number of timepoints\nfor all trials and sessions\" format requirement hold. Step 10 Check 5, item 6 pins down the\nhalf-open bin convention and notes that the independent sanity check uses the same convention.\n\n## 3-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Time from tone onset in seconds* derived from?\n\ni. `BehavioralEvents['sample_start_times'].timestamps` (the sample-epoch / instruction-tone\nonsets of the session) together with each trial's go-cue time. The tone assigned to a trial is\nthe **last** sample-epoch start at or before that trial's go cue, found with `searchsorted`.\nA trial with no preceding sample epoch raises a `RuntimeError` (never triggered).\n\nii.\n```python\n        # tone onset := last sample-epoch start before the go cue\n        sample_start = _events(nwb, 'sample_start_times')\n        tone_pos = np.searchsorted(sample_start, go, side='right') - 1\n        if np.any(tone_pos < 0):\n            raise RuntimeError(f'{session_id}: trial without a preceding sample epoch')\n        tone_time = sample_start[tone_pos]\n```\n\niii. Step 5 decision 8 and Step 10 Check 5, item 7: an early lick *replays* the sample epoch, so\na trial can carry more than one sample-start event; the last replay is the instruction the\nanimal actually acted on, and the one whose delay epoch leads to the go cue. The AI validated\nthis with the task geometry: the median tone→go interval is 1.85 s = 0.65 s sample + 1.2 s\ndelay, exactly the published structure, and it notes that on replay trials the residual delay\ncan be as short as 0.1 s, which is why the input is not a constant offset. Observed range over the full dataset: [−1.5, 11.9] s.\n\nii.\n```python\nBIN_CENTERS = BIN_EDGES[:-1] + BIN_SIZE / 2                   # (80,)\n```\n```python\n        # time from tone onset at each bin centre (seconds, continuous)\n        time_from_tone = BIN_CENTERS[None, :] + (go - tone_time)[:, None]   # (n_trials, NBINS)\n```\n```python\n    inputs = [np.stack([time_from_tone[j], photostim_on[j]]).astype(np.float32)\n              for j in range(n_trials)]\n```\n\niii. Step 5 decision 9: the task specification explicitly labels this input \"continuous,\ntime-varying\", which the AI read as overriding the general format note that \"if an input is a\ntime such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series\". Beyond locating the\ntone, no further processing is applied. How is the `input` *Time from tone onset in seconds* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. It is constructed *on* the neural bin grid: `BIN_CENTERS` are the centres of exactly the same\n80 bins whose edges (`BIN_EDGES`) are used to count spikes, laid on the same per-trial go-cue\ntimes (`go`, after trial curation). So alignment is structural — there is no separate\nalignment step, and bin *k* of the input necessarily covers the same interval as bin *k* of the\nfiring rates.\n\nii.\n```python\nBIN_EDGES = OFF_START + BIN_SIZE * np.arange(NBINS + 1)       # (81,)\nBIN_CENTERS = BIN_EDGES[:-1] + BIN_SIZE / 2                   # (80,)\n```\n```python\n    edges = go_times[:, None] + BIN_EDGES[None, :]            # neural\n```\n```python\n        time_from_tone = BIN_CENTERS[None, :] + (go - tone_time)[:, None]   # input\n```\n\niii. Step 10 Check 3(c): both streams are re-referenced to `go_start_times` on the single\nsession-absolute NWB clock, as in the reference `align_markers.py`. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Photostimulation* derived from?\n\ni. `BehavioralEvents['photostim_start_times'].timestamps` and\n`BehavioralEvents['photostim_stop_times'].timestamps` — the measured laser on/off times for the\nwhole session — together with each trial's go-cue time. The AI did *not* use the trials-table\n`photostim_onset` / `photostim_duration` string columns for the conversion, but did use them as\nan independent cross-check. Missing series are caught (`KeyError` → empty arrays) and a\nstart/stop count mismatch is warned about and leaves the input at 0.\n\nii.\n```python\n        photostim_on = np.zeros((n_trials, NBINS), dtype=np.float32)\n        try:\n            ps_start = _events(nwb, 'photostim_start_times')\n            ps_stop = _events(nwb, 'photostim_stop_times')\n        except KeyError:\n            ps_start = ps_stop = np.zeros(0)\n        if len(ps_start) and len(ps_start) == len(ps_stop):\n            for j, g in enumerate(go):\n                m = (ps_stop > g + OFF_START) & (ps_start < g + OFF_END)\n                if m.any():\n                    photostim_on[j] = interval_overlap_bins(ps_start[m], ps_stop[m], g)\n        elif len(ps_start) != len(ps_stop):\n            print(f'  WARNING {session_id}: photostim start/stop counts differ '\n                  f'({len(ps_start)}/{len(ps_stop)}); photostim input left at 0', flush=True)\n```\n\niii. Step 5 mapping: the reference analogue is `task_stimulation` columns 2–3, i.e. the laser\non/off *times*, which is exactly what the `BehavioralEvents` photostim series contain — so the\nAI chose the event stream over the derived trials-table strings. Sanity checks 6 and 7 verify\nthat the set of photostim trials derived from the event stream equals the set derived from the\nindependent `trials.photostim_onset != 'N/A'` column (exact match on 5 sessions), so the two\nsources agree. Check 8 verifies photostimulation always ends before the go cue and check 9 that\nonset lies inside the delay epoch on ≥ 98% of stim trials. Overall 20.0% of trials are\nstimulated, against ~19.6% in the raw data and \"~25% on photostim sessions\" in the papers.\n\n## 4-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Photostimulation*?\n\ni. A binary (0/1) `float32` time series, one value per bin: bin *k* is 1 if a photostim\ninterval overlaps it by **more than 1 ms** (`OVERLAP_TOL`), else 0. Overlap is computed\nvectorised over bins as `min(stop, edge_hi) − max(start, edge_lo)`; intervals entirely outside\nthe window are skipped. Trials with no stimulation keep an all-zero row.\n\nii.\n```python\nOVERLAP_TOL = 1e-3               # s, minimum overlap for a bin to count as photostim-on\n```\n```python\ndef interval_overlap_bins(starts, stops, go_time):\n    \"\"\"Binary (NBINS,) indicator: 1 where a [start, stop] interval overlaps the bin.\"\"\"\n    on = np.zeros(NBINS, dtype=np.float32)\n    if len(starts) == 0:\n        return on\n    for a, b in zip(starts - go_time, stops - go_time):\n        if b <= BIN_EDGES[0] or a >= BIN_EDGES[-1]:\n            continue\n        # Overlap duration between [a, b] and every bin.  A plain \"does it touch the bin\"\n        # test would mark a bin that the interval overlaps by a fraction of a millisecond:\n        # photoinhibition ends at the go cue to within +-0.5 ms, which would otherwise\n        # switch the first post-go bin on for about half of the stimulated trials.\n        ov = np.minimum(b, BIN_EDGES[1:]) - np.maximum(a, BIN_EDGES[:-1])\n        on[ov > OVERLAP_TOL] = 1.0\n    return on\n```\n\niii. Step 10 Check 2 records this as a bug the sanity checks caught and fixed: photoinhibition\nends at the go cue to within ±0.5 ms and starts within ±0.5 ms of a bin edge, so the original\n\"does the interval touch this bin\" test switched the first *post*-go bin on for about half the\nstimulated trials and turned on one bin too early at the onset. Requiring > 1 ms of overlap\nremoves the artefact and makes the \"photostim always ends before the go cue\" check pass\nexactly. The AI also verified, and documented as not-a-bug, one trial whose laser onset is\n2.25 s pre-go because an early-lick replay pushed the go cue later while the laser fired at its\nusual time. The `--show-processing` panel 5 shows the stimulation confined to the delay epoch\n(−1.2 to −0.7 s) on 77/354 trials in the sample session.\n\n## 4-c. How is the `input` *Photostimulation* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. Only intervals overlapping the trial's own [−2.5, +1.5] s window\nare considered. So alignment is again structural, on one shared grid.\n\nii.\n```python\n            for j, g in enumerate(go):\n                m = (ps_stop > g + OFF_START) & (ps_start < g + OFF_END)\n                if m.any():\n                    photostim_on[j] = interval_overlap_bins(ps_start[m], ps_stop[m], g)\n```\n```python\n    for a, b in zip(starts - go_time, stops - go_time):\n        ...\n        ov = np.minimum(b, BIN_EDGES[1:]) - np.maximum(a, BIN_EDGES[:-1])\n```\n\niii. Step 10 Check 3(e): the reference also re-references `task_stimulation` to the go cue; the\nonly difference is that the reference keeps it as per-trial scalars while this conversion\nrasterises it onto the bin grid, \"because the decoder wants time-varying inputs\". What processing is involved in computing `output` *Tongue y-position*?\n\ni. Four steps, all in `bin_tongue()`:\n1. Frames with DeepLabCut likelihood ≤ 0.9 are discarded — when the tongue is retracted the\n   tracker still reports a position, so those frames are not real measurements.\n2. Every frame is bucketed into the trial it was acquired in\n   (`searchsorted(trial_start, frame_t, 'right') - 1`), and frames belonging to trials that\n   were dropped by curation are discarded. A frame can therefore only contribute to *its own*\n   trial's window, never to a neighbour's.\n3. Surviving visible frames are mapped to `(trial, bin)` cells and the mean `y` per cell is\n   computed with two `np.bincount` calls (sums / counts).\n4. Do NOT look outside this project directory.\n\n**Goal**: Understand how the original authors loaded and processed their data.\n\n**Actions**:\n# Decisions\n\n## 1-a. How are **all the data** for all subjects, sessions, and trials loaded in?\n\ni. The dataset is distributed as one NWB file per session under `data/sub-<subject_id>/`. All sessions are found with a single glob over that layout, and each file is opened with `pynwb` and processed once. Subjects, trials, and units are then read from within each file (`nwb.subject`, `nwb.trials`, `nwb.units`, `nwb.acquisition`).\n\nii. Finding all data:\n```python\nfiles = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'sub-*', '*.nwb')))\n...\nfor i, path in enumerate(files, 1):\n    res = process_session(path)\n```\n\nLoading one session:\n```python\nwith NWBHDF5IO(path, mode='r', load_namespaces=True) as io:\n    nwb = io.read()\n    units = nwb.units\n    trials = nwb.trials.to_dataframe()\n    bev = nwb.acquisition['BehavioralEvents'].time_series\n```\n\niii. NWB is the published format for this dataset and `pynwb` is its standard reader. Since there is one file per session, the directory listing is the complete set of sessions and a glob is sufficient; sorting it makes the session order deterministic. The resulting counts (174 files, 28 subjects) match `assetsSummary` in `data/dandiset.yaml`.\n\n## 1-b. How are the data split into subjects?\n\ni. Each NWB file records its animal in `nwb.subject.subject_id`, a numeric string such as `'440956'`. That value is read for every session and carried through to assembly, where `subjects` is the sorted set of unique ids and `subject_idx` gives each session's index into that list.\n\nii. Per session:\n```python\nreturn {\n    'session_id': nwb.identifier,\n    'subject': nwb.subject.subject_id,\n    ...\n```\n\nAt assembly:\n```python\nsubjects = sorted({r['subject'] for r in results})\nsub_ix = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(subjects)}\n...\n'subjects': subjects,\n'subject_idx': np.array([sub_ix[r['subject']] for r in results], np.int32),\n```\n\niii. `subject_id` is the canonical animal identifier in the file, and the containing folder name (`sub-440956`) is derived from it, so no separate grouping step is needed. This gives 28 subjects with 3-10 sessions each, matching the dandiset. The numeric id differs from the mouse name used in the papers — `nwb.identifier` is e.g. `SC015_20190207_120657_s1`, so subject `440956` is mouse `SC015` — but the numeric id is what the NWB subject field provides, so it is used directly.\n\n## 1-c. How are the data split into sessions?\n\ni. One NWB file is one session, so no grouping or splitting is needed. Each session is identified by `nwb.identifier` (e.g. `SC015_20190207_120657_s1`, encoding mouse, date, time and session number), recorded per session and also listed in `metadata['session_info']`. Session order in the output follows the sorted file list.\n\nii.\n```python\nfiles = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'sub-*', '*.nwb')))\n```\n\n```python\n'session_id': nwb.identifier,\n```\n\n```python\n'session_info': [\n    {'session_id': r['session_id'], 'subject': r['subject'],\n     'n_trials': r['n_trials'], 'n_units': r['n_units']}\n    for r in results\n],\n```\n\niii. The dandiset already stores one session per file, so the file boundary is the session boundary and nothing has to be inferred. Because the filename embeds the acquisition timestamp (`sub-440956_ses-20190207T120657_...`), sorting the paths puts sessions in chronological order within each subject. 173 of the 174 files reach the output; the one exception is dropped for having no quality-controlled units (see 2-c).\n\n## 1-d. Are the data correctly split into trials?\n\ni. Trials come from the NWB trials table (`nwb.trials`), one row per behavioural trial, with exactly one go-cue event per row. The row count is checked against the number of go-cue events.\n\nii.\n```python\ntrials = nwb.trials.to_dataframe()\ngo = np.asarray(bev['go_start_times'].timestamps)\nassert len(go) == len(trials), f'{len(go)} go cues vs {len(trials)} trials'\n```\n\niii. Trials are clearly defined by the trials table, so it is used directly rather than re-deriving boundaries from the event streams. `go_start_times` has exactly one event per trial in all 174 sessions, which makes the mapping unambiguous. This is not true of the other trial-phase events: `sample_start_times` and `delay_start_times` can have several entries per trial, because a lick during the sample or delay replays that epoch.\n\n## 1-e. How are trials filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Trials are filtered only for absence of spike data, in two cases. First, trials outside `units/obs_intervals`: in 8 sessions the ephys recording starts after the behaviour, leaving up to 376 leading trials with no spikes. Second, `free_water` trials, which have no spikes anywhere in the window even though `obs_intervals` covers them. A session is dropped entirely if fewer than 2 trials survive. No behavioural quality filter is applied.\n\nii.\n```python\n# filter behavioral trials with no spike data\noi_off = np.asarray(units['obs_intervals'].data)\noi_start = np.concatenate([[0], oi_off[:-1]])\nobs = np.asarray(units['obs_intervals'].target.data)[oi_start[good[0]]:oi_off[good[0]]]\nkeep = np.isin(np.round(trials['start_time'].values, 4), np.round(obs[:, 0], 4))\nassert keep.sum() == len(obs), f'{keep.sum()} matched vs {len(obs)} observed'\n\n# filter no water trials\nkeep &= trials['free_water'].values == 0\nif keep.sum() < 2:\n    return None\ntrials = trials[keep]\ngo = go[keep]\n```\n\niii. `obs_intervals` is the file's own record of which trials were observed, and its start times match `trials.start_time`, which makes the mapping exact. The `free_water` exclusion was found empirically — those trials are covered by `obs_intervals` yet contain no spikes at all — and accounts for 2,449 of the 2,451 all-zero trials remaining after the `obs_intervals` filter.\n\nEarly-lick and no-response (`ignore`) trials are deliberately kept, even though the data paper states \"Early lick trials and no response trials were excluded for analysis\", because both are required decoder outputs here. The 2-trial minimum is the target format's requirement.\n\nTogether these remove 3,510 of the 94,370 trials in the retained sessions (3.7%), leaving 90,860.\n\n## 2-a. What variables in the raw data is the final `neural` data derived from?\n\ni. Neural data is derived from `units/spike_times`, the sorted spike times of each unit in session-absolute seconds. Only units with `classification == 'good'` contribute (see 2-c). The go-cue times (`BehavioralEvents/go_start_times`) are the other input, used to place the bin edges.\n\nii.\n```python\noffs = np.asarray(units['spike_times'].data)\nallst = np.asarray(units['spike_times'].target.data)\nstarts = np.concatenate([[0], offs[:-1]])\n\nedges = (go[:, None] + REL_EDGES[None, :]).ravel()\nrates = np.empty((good.size, n_trials, N_BINS), np.float32)\nfor r, u in enumerate(good):\n    s = allst[starts[u]:offs[u]]\n```\n\niii. `spike_times` is the only neural representation in the file, so firing rates are computed from it directly.\n\n## 2-b. How is the `neural` data processed?\n\ni. Spike times are converted to per-bin firing rates in Hz. For each good unit, the bin edges for every trial are built as one flat array of absolute times, `np.searchsorted` gives the running spike count at each edge, and differencing adjacent counts gives the spike count per bin. Counts are divided by the bin width to give Hz. No smoothing, normalisation, or baseline subtraction is applied.\n\nii.\n```python\nedges = (go[:, None] + REL_EDGES[None, :]).ravel()\nrates = np.empty((good.size, n_trials, N_BINS), np.float32)\nfor r, u in enumerate(good):\n    s = allst[starts[u]:offs[u]]\n    # running spike total at each edge; differencing gives the count per bin\n    pos = np.searchsorted(s, edges).reshape(n_trials, N_BINS + 1)\n    rates[r] = np.diff(pos, axis=1)\nrates /= BIN                                  # counts -> Hz\n```\n\niii. Firing rate is computed from the binned spike count over the 50 ms window defined in the instructions. This also matches the reference code, which calls `sliding_histogram(..., rate=True)` and returns `binSpikes / bin_width`.\n\n## 2-c. How is the `neural` data filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Only units with `units/classification == 'good'` are kept. No thresholds are applied to any individual quality metric. A session with no such units is dropped entirely. This retains 69,453 of 272,227 units (25.5%), a median of 390 per session.\n\nii.\n```python\n# ---- units: QC classifier verdict ----------------------------------\ncls = _text(units['classification'])\ngood = np.flatnonzero(cls == 'good')\nif good.size == 0:\n    return None\n```\n\niii. `classification` is the verdict of the spike-sorting quality-control classifier described in `ChenLiuEtAl2023_SpikeSortingQC.pdf`.\n\n`units/unit_quality` ('good' / 'multi') is deliberately not used: it is an older label that disagrees on 12.2% of the classifier-good units and is far more permissive.\n\nThe one dropped session (`sub-440958_ses-20190216T162508`) has `classification` and `anno_name` set to NaN for all 1,852 units, i.e. it was never quality-controlled. Excluding it gives 173 sessions and 69,453 good units, against the white paper's 173 sessions and 69,943 units.\n\n## 2-d. How is the per-trial `neural` data aligned to the event described in the `instructions`?\n\ni. Spike times and event times are already on the same session-absolute clock, so no alignment step is needed. The bin edges relative to the go cue are added to each trial's go-cue time to give the absolute time window for that trial, and the spikes are binned against those edges directly.\n\nii.\n```python\ngo = np.asarray(bev['go_start_times'].timestamps)\n```\n\n```python\nedges = (go[:, None] + REL_EDGES[None, :]).ravel()\nrates = np.empty((good.size, n_trials, N_BINS), np.float32)\nfor r, u in enumerate(good):\n    s = allst[starts[u]:offs[u]]\n    pos = np.searchsorted(s, edges).reshape(n_trials, N_BINS + 1)\n    rates[r] = np.diff(pos, axis=1)\n```\n\niii. Everything in the NWB file is timestamped on one global clock, so aligning to the go cue only requires looking up each trial's go-cue time and taking the window around it. There is no resampling or interpolation, and no per-stream offset to correct.\n\n## 2-e. How is the `neural` data temporally binned/resampled?\n\ni. Spike times are binned into 80 non-overlapping 50 ms bins spanning -2.5 s to +1.5 s relative to the go cue. The bin grid is defined once, as 81 edges relative to the go cue, and reused for every trial and session, so every trial has the same 80 timepoints.\n\nii.\n```python\n# trial window relative to the go cue, and bin width, in seconds\nT_START, T_STOP = -2.5, 1.5\nBIN = 0.05\nN_BINS = int(round((T_STOP - T_START) / BIN))             \n\nREL_EDGES = T_START + BIN * np.arange(N_BINS + 1)         \nCENTERS = REL_EDGES[:-1] + BIN / 2                        \n```\n\n```python\nedges = (go[:, None] + REL_EDGES[None, :]).ravel()\n```\n\niii. The window and the 50 ms bin width are set by the instructions. Defining the grid once as offsets from the go cue gives a constant 80 timepoints per trial, which the target format requires.\n\n## 3-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *time_from_tone_onset* derived from?\n\ni. From `sample_start_times`, the tone onsets of the session, together with the go cue of each trial. The tone taken for a trial is the **last one** before its go cue.\n\nii. The tone of each trial:\n```python\nsample = np.asarray(bev['sample_start_times'].timestamps)\ntone = sample[np.searchsorted(sample, go, side='left') - 1]\n```\n\niii. An early lick replays the sample epoch, so a trial can carry more than one tone; the last one before the go cue is the one the animal actually used.\n\n## 3-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *time_from_tone_onset*?\n\ni. The bins sit around the go cue, so the value of a bin is its center plus the gap between the tone and the go cue.\n\nii. The bin center, and the shift that turns them into time from the tone:\n```python\nCENTERS = REL_EDGES[:-1] + BIN / 2                        \n```\n```python\n# bins sit around the go cue, values are seconds since the tone\ntime_from_tone = CENTERS[None, :] + (go - tone)[:, None]\n```\n\niii. No additional processing needed other than find the tone onset time.\n\n## 3-c. How is `input` *time_from_tone_onset* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. It is how the neural binnning grid is defined.\n\nii. The grid, defined once as offsets from the go cue, and laid on each trial's go cue to bin the spikes:\n```python\nT_START, T_STOP = -2.5, 1.5\nBIN = 0.05\nN_BINS = int(round((T_STOP - T_START) / BIN))             \n\nREL_EDGES = T_START + BIN * np.arange(N_BINS + 1)         \nCENTERS = REL_EDGES[:-1] + BIN / 2                        \n```\n```python\nedges = (go[:, None] + REL_EDGES[None, :]).ravel()\n```\n\niii. N/A\n\n## 4-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *photostim* derived from?\n\ni. From `photostim_onset` and `photostim_duration` in the trials table, with `start_time` and the go cue used to place them on the trial's time axis.\n\nii. The onset and offset of the stimulation, relative to the go cue:\n```python\non_s = trials['photostim_onset'].values\nhas = on_s != 'N/A'\nstim_on[has] = trials['start_time'].values[has] + on_s[has].astype(float) - go[has]\nstim_off[has] = stim_on[has] + trials['photostim_duration'].values[has].astype(float)\n```\n\niii. The onsets are stored as strings measured from trial start, with `'N/A'` on the trials that were not stimulated, so they have to be converted and re-expressed against the go cue the bins are aligned on.\n\n## 4-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *photostim*?\n\ni. A bin is 1 where its center falls between the onset and the offset of the stimulation and 0 elsewhere, so the input is a binary time series rather than a per trial flag.\n\nii. The bins the light is on for:\n```python\n# NaN compares False, so non-stim trials stay 0\nphotostim = ((CENTERS[None, :] >= stim_on[:, None])\n             & (CENTERS[None, :] < stim_off[:, None]))\n```\n\niii. A trial without stimulation keeps NaN bounds, and NaN compares false, so all of its bins come out 0 without a separate branch.\n\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Convert the Brain-wide Activity Map dataset (DANDI 000363) to the decoder format.\n\n    python -u convert_data.py <outpicklefile> [--full | --sample] [--datadir DIR]\n\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nimport glob\nimport os\nimport pickle\nimport re\nimport sys\nimport time\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom pynwb import NWBHDF5IO\n\n_chen2024_seed = 'x5cidj2hy87s'\nnp.random.seed(sum(ord(c) for c in _chen2024_seed) % 2**31)\n\nHERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))\n# Default only, for running this by hand from manual/chen2024/. The oracle arm runs\n# the script from /solution while the dataset is mounted read-only at /app/data, so\n# solve.sh overrides this with --datadir.\nDATA_DIR = os.path.join(HERE, 'data')\n\n# trial window relative to the go cue, and bin width, in seconds\nT_START, T_STOP = -2.5, 1.5\nBIN = 0.05\nN_BINS = int(round((T_STOP - T_START) / BIN))             # 80\n\nREL_EDGES = T_START + BIN * np.arange(N_BINS + 1)         # 81 edges, re go cue\nCENTERS = REL_EDGES[:-1] + BIN / 2                        # 80 bin centres\n\nOUTCOME_CODE = {'ignore': 0, 'miss': 1, 'hit': 2}\nEARLY_CODE = {'no early': 0, 'early': 1}\nSIDE_CODE = {'left': 0, 'right': 1}\nCHOICE_NO_LICK = 2               # no lick in the response window\nTONGUE_HIDDEN = 3                # no visible tongue frame in the bin\n\nTONGUE_CONF = 0.5                # tracking likelihood for the tongue to count as visible\nTONGUE_PCT = (40, 60)            # per-session percentiles -> 3 visible classes\n\nINPUT_NAMES = ['time_from_tone_onset', 'photostim']\nOUTPUT_NAMES = ['choice', 'outcome', 'early_lick', 'tongue_y_position']\n\n# output_values[i][code] names each value of output i\nOUTPUT_VALUES = [\n    ['left', 'right', 'no lick'],\n    ['ignore', 'miss', 'hit'],\n    ['no', 'yes'],\n    ['below 40th pct', '40th to 60th pct', 'above 60th pct', 'not visible'],\n]\n\n\ndef region_label(anno):\n    \"\"\"'Orbital area, lateral part, layer 5' -> 'orbital area'.\"\"\"\n    return re.split(r'[,./]', anno)[0].strip().lower()\n\n\ndef _text(col):\n    \"\"\"Read a text column; non-str entries (unlabelled sessions) become ''.\"\"\"\n    return np.array([x if isinstance(x, str) else '' for x in col[:]])\n\n\ndef _bin_mean(idx, y, n):\n    \"\"\"Mean of y per bin given a per-sample bin index. NaN where a bin is empty.\"\"\"\n    ok = ~np.isnan(y)\n    tot = np.bincount(idx[ok], weights=y[ok], minlength=n)\n    cnt = np.bincount(idx[ok], minlength=n)\n    with np.errstate(invalid='ignore'):\n        return np.where(cnt > 0, tot / np.maximum(cnt, 1), np.nan)\n\n\ndef tongue_output(nwb, go):\n    \"\"\"Discretise tongue y into (n_trials, N_BINS) classes.\"\"\"\n    ts = nwb.acquisition['BehavioralTimeSeries'].time_series['Camera0_side_TongueTracking']\n    t_cam = np.asarray(ts.timestamps)\n    data = ts.data[:]                        # (n_frames, 3) = x, y, likelihood\n    y = data[:, 1].copy()\n    y[data[:, 2] < TONGUE_CONF] = np.nan     # keep only visible frames\n\n    # bin the whole session on one grid, then take percentiles of the bin means\n    gidx = np.floor((t_cam - t_cam[0]) / BIN).astype(np.int64)\n    edges = np.nanpercentile(_bin_mean(gidx, y, int(gidx[-1]) + 1), TONGUE_PCT)\n\n    # per trial, bin the same way and digitise against those edges\n    cls = np.full((len(go), N_BINS), TONGUE_HIDDEN, np.int8)\n    lo = np.searchsorted(t_cam, go + T_START, 'left')\n    hi = np.searchsorted(t_cam, go + T_STOP, 'left')\n    for i in range(len(go)):\n        b = np.floor((t_cam[lo[i]:hi[i]] - (go[i] + T_START)) / BIN).astype(np.int64)\n        np.clip(b, 0, N_BINS - 1, out=b)\n        m = _bin_mean(b, y[lo[i]:hi[i]], N_BINS)\n        ok = ~np.isnan(m)\n        cls[i, ok] = np.digitize(m[ok], edges)\n    return cls\n\n\ndef process_session(path):\n    \"\"\"Convert one NWB file. Returns a dict, or None if the session is dropped.\"\"\"\n    with NWBHDF5IO(path, mode='r', load_namespaces=True) as io:\n        nwb = io.read()\n        units = nwb.units\n        trials = nwb.trials.to_dataframe()\n        bev = nwb.acquisition['BehavioralEvents'].time_series\n\n        # ---- units: QC classifier verdict ----------------------------------\n        cls = _text(units['classification'])\n        good = np.flatnonzero(cls == 'good')\n        if good.size == 0:\n            return None\n        regions = [region_label(a) for a in _text(units['anno_name'])[good]]\n\n        # all NWB times are session-absolute seconds\n        go = np.asarray(bev['go_start_times'].timestamps)\n        assert len(go) == len(trials), f'{len(go)} go cues vs {len(trials)} trials'\n\n        # ---- trials filtering ----\n        # spike data\n        # obs_intervals gives one [start, stop] per observed trial, which in some\n        # sessions is fewer than the behavioural trials. \n        # a behavioural trial is observed if its start time is one of the interval starts\n        obs = np.asarray(units['obs_intervals'][good[0]])        \n        keep = np.isin(trials['start_time'].values, obs[:, 0])\n        assert keep.sum() == len(obs), f'{keep.sum()} matched vs {len(obs)} observed'\n\n        # filter no water trials\n        keep &= trials['free_water'].values == 0\n        \n        # a sessioon has to have at least 2 trials according to the instruction\n        if keep.sum() < 2:\n            return None\n        \n        trials = trials[keep]\n        go = go[keep]\n        n_trials = len(go)\n\n        # last tone onset before the go cue; \"\"\"Binary (NBINS,) indicator: 1 where a [start, stop] interval overlaps the bin.\n\n    Args:\n        starts, stops: absolute start/stop times of the intervals (may be empty).\n        go_time: t1\n\n        # ---------------- outputs --------------------------------------------------\n        t1 = time.time()\n        instr_k = instruction[keep_idx]\n        out_k = outcome[keep_idx]\n        early_k = early_lick[keep_idx]\n\n        # choice: hit -> instructed side, miss -> opposite side, ignore -> no lick\n        choice = np.full(n_trials, CHOICE_NOLICK, dtype=np.int64)\n        hit = out_k == 'hit'\n        miss = out_k == 'miss'\n        choice[hit & (instr_k == 'left')] = CHOICE_LEFT\n        choice[hit & (instr_k == 'right')] = CHOICE_RIGHT\n        choice[miss & (instr_k == 'left')] = CHOICE_RIGHT\n        choice[miss & (instr_k == 'right')] = CHOICE_LEFT\n\n        outcome_code = np.array([OUTCOME_CODE[o] for o in out_k], dtype=np.int64)\n        early_code = (early_k == 'early').astype(np.int64)\n\n        tongue_y_binned, tongue_visible_frac = bin_tongue(nwb, trial_start, go, keep_idx)\n        tongue_class, pct = discretise_tongue(tongue_y_binned)\n        timing['output'] = time.time() - t1\n\n        io.close()\n\n    # ---------------- assemble ----------------------------------------------------\n    neural = [fr[:, j, :] for j in range(n_trials)]\n    inputs = [np.stack([time_from_tone[j], photostim_on[j]]).astype(np.float32)\n              for j in range(n_trials)]\n    outputs = [np.stack([np.full(NBINS, choice[j]),\n                         np.full(NBINS, outcome_code[j]),\n                         np.full(NBINS, early_code[j]),\n                         tongue_class[j]]).astype(np.int64)\n               for j in range(n_trials)]\n\n    result = dict(\n        session_id=session_id,\n        subject=subject,\n        file=os.path.basename(path),\n        neural=neural,\n        input=inputs,\n        output=outputs,\n        brain_region_idx=region_idx,\n        hemisphere=np.where(hemisphere == 'left', 0, 1).astype(np.int8),\n        n_trials_raw=n_trials_raw,\n        n_trials_observed=n_trials_obs,\n        n_trials=n_trials,\n        n_neurons=n_neurons,\n        trial_index=keep_idx,                     # index into the raw trials table\n        tongue_percentiles=pct,\n        tongue_visible_frac=float(tongue_visible_frac),\n        timing=timing,\n        total_time=time.time() - t0,\n    )\n    if collect_debug:\n        result['debug'] = dict(\n            go=go, tone_time=tone_time, trial_start=trial_start[keep_idx],\n            trial_stop=trial_stop[keep_idx], time_from_tone=time_from_tone,\n            photostim_on=photostim_on, tongue_y=tongue_y_binned, tongue_class=tongue_class,\n            fr=fr, instruction=instr_k, outcome=out_k, early=early_k,\n            choice=choice, anno=anno, region_name=region_name, hemisphere=hemisphere,\n# Dataset Conversion Notes\n\n## Overview\n- **Dataset**: MAP (Mesoscale Activity Project) brain-wide Neuropixels dataset.\n  - Data paper: Chen, Liu, et al. *Brain-wide neural activity underlying memory-guided movement*, Cell 187, 676–691 (2024). (`/app/datapaper.pdf`)\n  - Method paper: Wang, Kurgyis, et al. *Brain-wide analysis reveals movement encoding structured across and within brain areas*, Nat Neurosci (2025). (`/app/methodpaper.pdf`)\n  - Spike-sorting/QC white paper: `/app/ChenLiuEtAl2023_SpikeSortingQC.pdf`\n  - Source: DANDI:000363, NWB 2.x files in `/app/data` (174 files, 28 subjects, ~50 GB).\n- **Date started**: 2026-09-20\n- **Goal**: Convert to decoder-compatible format (`/app/converted_data.pkl`)\n\n---\n\n## Step 0: Setup and Initialization\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\nDirectory contents of `/app`:\n- `CONVERSION_NOTES.md` (this file)\n- `datapaper.pdf`, `methodpaper.pdf`, `ChenLiuEtAl2023_SpikeSortingQC.pdf`, `methods.txt`\n- `code/` — reference analysis code for the method paper (MapVideoAnalysis repo)\n- `data/` — 29 `sub-*` directories, 174 `*.nwb` files (50 GB total)\n- `pynwb_docs/` — local copy of pynwb documentation\n- `decoder.py`, `train_decoder.py` — provided decoder/validation code\n- `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yaml`, `.manifest`\n\nEnvironment check: `python3` works; `numpy 2.4.4`, `torch 2.6.0+cu124` (CUDA available,\n23 GB GPU), `pynwb 4.1.0`. Machine has 128 cores / 1 TB RAM.\n\n---\n\n## Step 1: Reference Code Exploration\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\nThe reference repository (`/app/code`) is the analysis code of the *method paper*. It does not\nread NWB directly — it reads `.mat` files exported from the Janelia DataJoint pipeline. The\nDataJoint export and the NWB release contain the same underlying quantities, so the reference\ncode tells us **which** variables are used and **how** they are processed.\n\n### Key Functions Identified\n| Function | File | Stage | Purpose |\n|----------|------|-------|---------|\n| `preprocessing_utils.loadmat` | `VideoAnalysisUtils/preprocessing_utils.py` | LOADING | Load one probe's `.mat` export (replaced here by `pynwb`) |\n| `preprocessing.process_one_sess` | `VideoAnalysisUtils/preprocessing_DJ_2022Aug.py` | LOADING/CURATION | Concatenate all probes of a session; `rate=True` ⇒ divide by `bw` to get **firing rate in Hz** |\n| `Sherlock/preprocess_all_ephys.py` | — | PROCESSING | Top-level parameters actually used for the paper: `bw = 0.04`, `stride = 0.0034`, `begin_time = -3.0`, `end_time = 3.0`, `qc_mode = 'classifier'` |\n| `functions_for_r2.get_regular_trial_mask` / `population_decoding_utils.get_regular_trial_mask` | `VideoAnalysisUtils/…` | CURATION | Trial mask: `early_lick == 0`, `auto_water == 0`, `free_water == 0`, `correctness != -1` (no-response), `stimulation[:,0] == 0` (no photostim) |\n| `functions_for_r2.create_4fold_trial_type_mask` | `VideoAnalysisUtils/functions_for_r2.py` | PROCESSING | Defines the (trial_type, correctness) contingencies used for stratification; Cells **do** have to be quality-filtered.\n- Quality control is `qc_mode='classifier'`: the region-specific logistic-regression classifiers\n  described in `methods.txt` and the QC white paper. Their output is a per-unit `'good'` /\n  `'unlabelled'` label. In NWB this is the `units.classification` column — no need to re-derive\n  it from the 15 raw quality metrics (which are also present in the file).\n- The reference also requires a unit to have a CCF annotation (`ccf_label[idx] != []`). In NWB,\n  `units.anno_name` is non-empty **exactly** for units with `classification == 'good'`\n  (verified: 0 good units with empty annotation, 0 unlabelled units with an annotation, in the\n  example session), so the two criteria coincide.\n- Hemisphere rule (reference): CCF `x >= 5700 µm` ⇒ left hemisphere, else right.\n- Brain areas used by the reference (14): `ALM, Medulla, Midbrain, Striatum, Thalamus, Pons,\n  Cerebellum, Hypothalamus, Hippocampus, Orbital, OtherCortex, Olfactory, CorticalSubplate,\n  Pallidum`, each split into `left_`/`right_`.\n- Spike times in the reference `.mat` export are **already relative to the go cue**; in NWB they\n  are absolute session times, so we must subtract `go_start_times` ourselves.\n- The reference bins with *sliding* windows (40 ms width, 3.4 ms stride) because it needs the\n  neural signal on the 300 Hz video grid. Our task specifies **50 ms bins**, so we use\n  non-overlapping 50 ms bins (width = stride = 50 ms) and keep `rate=True` (Hz), which is the\n  only deviation from `sliding_histogram`.\n\n---\n\n## Step 2: Dataset Exploration\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Data Structure\n```\n/app/data/\n  dandiset.yaml\n  sub-<subject_id>/                      # 29 dirs, 28 of them subjects (+ dandiset.yaml)\n    sub-<id>_ses-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSS>_behavior+ecephys+ogen.nwb\n```\n174 NWB files, one per behavioural session. `obs_intervals` — `(n_trials, 2)`, exactly equal to\n    the trials table `start_time`/`stop_time` and identical for every unit in a session.\n- `nwb.acquisition['BehavioralEvents']` — `TimeSeries` whose *timestamps* carry the events:\n  `presample/sample/delay/go/trialend _start_times` and `_stop_times`,\n  `left_lick_times`, `right_lick_times`, `photostim_start_times` (`data` = power in mW),\n  `photostim_stop_times`. `go_start_times` has exactly one timestamp per trial in all 174 files.\n- `nwb.acquisition['BehavioralTimeSeries']` — DeepLabCut markers, absolute timestamps, 300 Hz:\n  `Camera0_side_JawTracking`, `Camera0_side_NoseTracking`, `Camera0_side_TongueTracking`\n  (each `(n_frames, 3)` = `x, y, likelihood`). Present in **all 174 sessions**.\n  20 sessions additionally have `Camera0_side_WhiskerTracking_whisker`, 4 have\n  `Camera0_side_LickPortTracking`, 3 have a second camera `Camera3_side_*`.\n- `nwb.electrodes` — CCF coordinates `x,y,z` per electrode; `nwb.electrode_groups[*].location`\n  is a JSON string with the *targeted* `brain_regions` (e.g. `\"left ALM\"`) and stereotaxic\n  coordinates.\n\n### Dataset Size (from data files)\n| Statistic | Value |\n|-----------|-------|\n| NWB files (sessions) | 174 |\n| Sessions with ≥1 `good` unit | **173** |\n| Subjects | **28** |\n| Sessions / subject | mean 6.2 (range 4–9) |\n| Probe insertions (electrode groups) | 659 total; The reference `.mat` export\n  stores spike times already relative to the go cue; markers are aligned by subtracting\n  `task_cue_time[0]` (= go cue) (`align_markers.py`).\n- **Windows**: reference ephys window `[-3.0, 3.0]` s (script) / `[-3.0, 3.5]` s (module default)\n  around the go cue; marker window `[-3, 1.5)` s.\n- **Binning**: firing **rates** (Hz) = counts / bin width.\n- **Markers**: outliers detected with a 5σ threshold on inter-frame velocity and imputed from\n  neighbouring frames; \"when the tongue was occluded while it was in the mouth … we set the tongue\n  position to its mean value\" — i.e. *tongue occlusion is explicitly a distinct state*, which is\n  exactly the \"not visible\" class (3) required here.\n\n### Curation Steps\n\n**Neuron curation rules**\n- Kilosort2 output → 15 quality metrics → five region-specific logistic-regression classifiers →\n  label `good` / `unlabelled`. Only `good` units are analysed (⇒ `classification == 'good'`).\n- Reference additionally requires a valid CCF annotation (equivalent in NWB, see Step 1).\n- Method paper only: neurons with mean firing rate < 2 Hz excluded *from the firing-rate\n  prediction (R²) analyses*; explicitly stated to be insensitive to the threshold.\n- Recordings with substantial drift were rejected at the penetration level (QC white paper); the\n  residue of this manual annotation is the per-insertion `is_good_trials` vector.\n\n**Trial curation rules**\n- Data paper: \"Early lick trials and no response trials were excluded for analysis.\"\n- Method paper: \"The dataset contains trials with photoinhibition, water administration regardless\n  of the animals' choice (free water trials), early licks and trials where the animal ignores the\n  lick-spouts. These were excluded from all analyses.\"\n- Reference code `get_regular_trial_mask`: `early_lick == 0 & auto_water == 0 & free_water == 0 &\n  correctness != -1 & stimulation == 0`.\n\n### Decoders Trained (accuracies reported in the papers)\n| Decoded variable | Method | Accuracy |\n|---|---|---|\n| Choice (lick left/right), from **video** embedding, response epoch | logistic regression | ROC AUC 0.99 ± 0.01 (n = 106 sessions) |\n| Choice from video, sample epoch (2nd half) | logistic regression | AUC ≈ 0.6 (highly variable across sessions) |\n| Choice from video, pre-sample | — | AUC 0.51 ± 0.06 (chance) |\n| Choice from video markers, response epoch | logistic regression | 0.88 ± 0.01 |\n| Choice (lick left/right) from **neural** pseudo-populations (200 neurons/area) | logistic regression, nested 5-fold CV | ≈ 0.9–1.0 after the go cue; rises through sample/delay (data paper Fig 6D) |\n| Single-neuron choice selectivity | d′ / AUC | AUC > 0.65 used as \"choice-modulated\" threshold |\n\nNo paper reports decoding of `outcome`, `early lick` or `tongue position` from neural activity,\nso there is no direct published accuracy target for three of the four outputs. Choice decoding\nfrom a full simultaneously-recorded population after the go cue should be near-perfect\n(≥ 0.9 balanced accuracy) if the conversion is correct.\n\n---\n\n## Step 4: Check for Consistency\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Discrepancies Found\n| Topic | Code says | Data shows | Papers say | Resolution |\n|-------|-----------|------------|------------|------------|\n| Number of sessions | — | 174 NWB files, **173** with ≥ 1 good unit | 173 behavioral sessions | The file `SC017_20190216_162508_s4` has 0 good units (4 insertions). The upper end matches (0.989 ≈ 99 %). 16–23 sessions fall below the stated 65 % criterion. Since the *session* and *insertion* counts match the paper exactly, the DANDI release **is** the analysed set; the published selection criteria were applied at an earlier stage / on a slightly different definition. ⇒ **do not** re-apply a performance filter (it would remove sessions the authors kept). |\n| Photostim fraction | `stimulation[:,0] != 0` | 18,588 / 94,990 = **19.6 %** of trials | \"~25 % randomly interleaved\" (17/25 mice) | Consistent: not every session/mouse had photostimulation, and the quoted 25 % is per photostim session. |\n| Trial exclusions | exclude early-lick, no-response, photostim, auto-water, free-water | — | same | **Conflict with the decoder task**: `early lick` and `outcome (ignore)` are required decoder *outputs* and photostimulation is a required decoder *input*. These three exclusions are therefore dropped. Auto-water and free-water trials have no such requirement and are excluded, as in the reference. |\n| `outcome` semantics | `correctness` 1 = correct, 0 = error, −1 = no response | verified against lick times: on `hit` trials the animal licks the instructed port (100 %), on `miss` trials it *first* licks the opposite port (100 %), on `ignore` trials there are no licks in [go, go+1.5] (100 %) | hit / miss / ignore | Confirmed; `choice` can be derived from (`trial_instruction`, `outcome`). |\n| Observation window | reference truncates spikes to a fixed window around the go cue and bins the whole window | `obs_intervals` == trials `[start_time, stop_time]`; **no spikes exist outside them** | — | The per-trial recorded interval covers `go − 3.15 s` (median) to `go + 1.80 s` (median). 96.9 % of trials cover −2.5 s and 84.4 % cover +1.5 s. On error (`miss`) trials the interval ends at the error lick, so only 8 % of miss trials reach go+1.5 s. The reference does the same thing we will do — bin the full fixed window, which yields zeros where nothing was recorded. Documented as a known caveat (it makes `outcome` partly decodable from the zero-padding). |\n| Tongue tracking availability | method paper used 105–106 sessions | `Camera0_side_TongueTracking` present in **all 174** sessions | \"105/106 sessions\" | The method paper additionally required a usable *raw video* (for the autoencoder/end-to-end pipelines) and `align_markers.py` skips sessions missing any of 8 markers (incl. whisker). DLC tongue markers are available everywhere, so no session needs to be dropped for the tongue output. |\n\n---\n\n## Step 5: Mapping Planning\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Variable Mapping\n| Source (NWB) | Target field | Transform | Reference analogue |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `units.spike_times` (absolute) + `BehavioralEvents.go_start_times.timestamps` | `neural` | subtract go-cue time per trial; keep spikes in `[-2.5, 1.5)`; histogram into 80 non-overlapping 50 ms bins; divide by 0.05 ⇒ Hz | `process_one_area` + `sliding_histogram(rate=True)` |\n| `units.classification == 'good'` | neuron filter | keep only `good` | `idx_qc_dict` (`qc_mode='classifier'`) |\n| `units.anno_name` + electrode CCF `x` | `brain_regions`, `brain_region_idx` | map Allen annotation → one of 14 coarse regions; hemisphere from `x >= 5700` | `helper_get_neuron_id_area` |\n| `BehavioralEvents.sample_start_times` (last one before the go cue) | `input[0]` `time_from_tone_onset_s` | `t_bin_center − t_tone`, seconds, continuous | `task_sample_time` |\n| `BehavioralEvents.photostim_start_times` / `photostim_stop_times` | `input[1]` `photostim_on` | 1 if the photostim interval overlaps the bin, else 0 | `task_stimulation` cols 2–3 |\n| `trials.trial_instruction` + `trials.outcome` | `output[0]` `lick_direction_choice` | hit ⇒ instructed side; miss ⇒ opposite side; ignore ⇒ no lick. 0 = left, 1 = right, 2 = no lick | `lick_directions` / `correctness` |\n| `trials.outcome` | `output[1]` `outcome` | 0 = ignore, 1 = miss, 2 = hit | `correctness` (−1/0/1) |\n| `trials.early_lick` | `output[2]` `early_lick` | 0 = no, 1 = yes | `behavior_early_report` |\n| `BehavioralTimeSeries.Camera0_side_TongueTracking` (`y`, `likelihood`) | `output[3]` `tongue_y_position` | per 50 ms bin: mean `y` over frames of *that trial* with `likelihood > 0.9`; if no such frame ⇒ 3 (not visible); else 0/1/2 by session percentiles (<40th, 40–60th, >60th) | `tracking.camera_0_side.tongue_y` |\n| `nwb.subject.subject_id` | `subjects`, `subject_idx` | unique sorted list | — |\n| `trials.auto_water`, `trials.free_water` | trial filter | drop | `get_regular_trial_mask` |\n| `units.is_good_trials` | trial filter | drop trials flagged `False` for any retained unit | drift QC (white paper) |\n\n### Key Decisions\n1. **Alignment = go cue** (`BehavioralEvents['go_start_times'].timestamps`, one per trial).\n   Matches both papers and all reference code.\n2. **Window = [−2.5, +1.5] s, 80 non-overlapping 50 ms bins** (task spec). Bin *k* covers\n   `[-2.5 + 0.05k, -2.5 + 0.05(k+1))`, centre `-2.475 + 0.05k`.\n3. **Firing rates in Hz** (counts / 0.05 s), as `sliding_histogram(rate=True)`.\n4. **Neuron filter: `classification == 'good'` only.** This is exactly the classifier-based QC of\n   the data paper. The method paper's extra \"≥ 2 Hz\" filter is *not* applied: it was introduced to\n   stabilise per-neuron R² estimates in the video→firing-rate regression, not for decoding, and\n   discarding low-rate neurons would throw away decodable information.\n5. **Trial filter**: drop `auto_water` and `free_water` trials (reference); drop trials not\n   flagged good in `is_good_trials` for any retained unit (drift QC). **Keep** early-lick,\n   `ignore`, and photostim trials — required by the decoder input/output spec.\n6. **Session filter**: drop sessions with 0 good units (1 session) and sessions with < 2 trials\n   after curation. No behavioural-performance filter (see Step 4).\n7. **Zero padding outside the recorded interval** is kept rather than dropping trials, matching\n   `process_one_area`, because dropping would remove ~92 % of `miss` trials and destroy the\n   `outcome` output. Documented caveat.\n8. **Tone onset = last `sample_start_time` before the go cue** — with early licks the sample epoch\n   is replayed, and the last replay is the instruction that actually precedes the delay/go.\n   Median tone→go = 1.85 s (= 0.65 s sample + 1.2 s delay), as expected from the task design.\n9. **`time_from_tone_onset` is a continuous ramp** (explicitly required by the task spec:\n   \"continuous, time-varying\"), not a binary indicator.\n10. **Tongue visibility threshold: DLC likelihood > 0.9.** The likelihood distribution is\n    strongly bimodal (≈ 3–6 × 10⁻⁵ vs ≈ 1.0); any threshold in [0.1, 0.99] gives the same answer\n    to within 0.1 % of frames. ~6–11 % of frames have the tongue visible.\n11. **Tongue percentiles are computed per session** over the *binned, visible* values of all\n    retained trials of that session (the quantity actually being discretised).\n12. **Per-trial outputs are broadcast across time**, because the output array must have a single\n    shape and the tongue output is time-varying.\n13. **Brain regions: 14 coarse areas** (the reference's list). ALM is defined as units on\n    ALM-targeted insertions annotated to secondary motor / primary motor / frontal-pole areas.\n    Hemisphere is stored separately in metadata rather than doubling the region list.\n\n### Planned Sanity Checks\n- [ ] 173 sessions, 28 subjects, 655 insertions, ≈ 69.4 k good units.\n- [ ] Trials/session (excluding early licks) ≈ 476.\n- [ ] Photostim trials ≈ 20 % of trials; photostim always ends before the go cue and lies in the\n      delay epoch.\n- [ ] Median tone→go interval = 1.85 s.\n- [ ] `choice` derived from (instruction, outcome) agrees with the direction of the **first lick**\n      after the go cue on ≥ 99 % of hit/miss trials, and `ignore` trials have no licks.\n- [ ] Tongue visible ≈ 6–11 % of frames; visible bins concentrated after the go cue.\n- [ ] Tongue class fractions ≈ 40 / 20 / 40 of the *visible* bins.\n- [ ] Per-neuron mean firing rate in the converted data matches `units.avg_firing_rate` in order\n      of magnitude, and a direct spike-count recomputation from the raw NWB matches exactly.\n- [ ] Neural, input and output spot-checks against the raw NWB with `np.allclose`.\n\n---\n\n## Step 6: Script Development\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n`/app/convert_data.py` (+ `/app/ccf_regions.py` for the CCF annotation → coarse-area map).\n\nStructure:\n- `list_session_files()` — enumerate the 174 NWB files.\n- `process_session(path)` — everything for one session; returns `None` if the session is dropped.\n- `bin_spikes_rate(spike_times, go_times)` — vectorised binning.
